Action Plan:
1. Start prescribed antibiotic course for suspected urinary tract infection: take twice daily for 3 days; prescription sent to patient’s nominated pharmacy (antibiotic name/dose/route not documented).
2. Safety-netting: seek urgent care or re-contact service if abdominal pain worsens, fever develops, back/flank pain occurs, new symptoms arise, or if symptoms do not improve; may require face-to-face examination.
3. Re-contact if symptoms recur after completing antibiotics.
4. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: 2-day history of lower abdominal (central/lower tummy) pain; feels hot and sweaty.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Nausea (mild), no vomiting.
  - Urinary: slight pink discoloration in urine (patient-reported hematuria), increased frequency “a little bit,” increased thirst. Denies dysuria earlier; later acknowledged “difficulty when passing urine” when prompted (conflict noted).
  - Bowel: constipation last week, now resolved; last bowel movement 2 hours ago, normal; no blood in stool.
  - Gynecologic: regular periods; no intermenstrual or post-coital bleeding; no abnormal vaginal discharge. Previously had an internal contraceptive implant, removed ~1 year ago.
  - Systemic: feels sweaty; temperature measured 1 hour prior was ~37°C; no documented fever.
  - No back pain. No recent travel.
- Past medical history: No significant medical problems reported.
- Medications: None regular. No OTC use reported.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction not documented).
- Family history: Mother with breast cancer (treated early).
- Social history: Lives with parents. Non-smoker. Alcohol ~1 beer, ~4 times per week.

Objective:
- Vitals (patient-reported): Temperature ~37°C measured 1 hour prior.
- Physical exam: Telehealth visit; no in-person exam performed.
- Investigations: None performed or ordered during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain with urinary symptoms and hematuria:
   - Assessment: Suspected acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis).
   - Differential diagnosis (limited): Nephrolithiasis; urethritis; less likely early pyelonephritis (no fever/back pain reported).
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned: Empiric antibiotics prescribed, to be taken twice daily for 3 days; antibiotic name/dose/route not documented. Prescription to patient’s nominated pharmacy.
   - Safety net: If pain worsens, fever or back pain develops, new/worsening symptoms occur, or no improvement, contact service urgently; may require face-to-face examination. Re-contact if symptoms recur after treatment.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No urinalysis or urine culture ordered; pregnancy status not assessed; no pain severity scale; antibiotic name/dose/route not documented; allergy reaction details not documented; no vitals beyond patient-reported temperature; no follow-up appointment timeframe specified.
- Internal conflicts: Patient denied dysuria earlier but later agreed when asked about difficulty passing urine (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Portions were unclear/fragmented; some responses were difficult to interpret.
